title: Monoscheme resolution rules and sharpening comparison data
statement:
Use fine monoschemes, their local smooth morphisms, coherent monoid ideals, sharpening and saturated blowup towers from [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], and fine fans, smooth-functorial fan resolutions and ordered contraction from [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. A monoscheme resolution input is a fine monoscheme $M$ with a finite affine cover and with torsion-free group completions of both its ordinary and its sharp stalk monoids. A resolution is a finite saturated blowup tower with an identification of its initial object with $M$ and smooth last object. A comparison over $g:N\to M$ is a recursive pullback of the target tower to $N$, together with a center-preserving contraction to the source tower, pinned over $g$. Its level map is the inverse of the contraction isomorphism followed by the pullback lift. A smooth-functorial monoscheme resolution rule assigns these resolutions and comparisons for every input and smooth map, with identity and composition equations for both contraction indices and actual level maps. A fan tower identification is an order-preserving bijection of level indices, preserving first and last indices, with level isomorphisms commuting with arrows and pulling back every center exactly.

Let $\lambda$ be quotient by units followed by sheafification. On ideals its image consists of sections locally lifted from the original ideal, and inverse image is sectionwise inverse image under $\lambda$. A sharpened map has the same underlying continuous map and commutes with $\lambda$ on sections; use the uniquely determined such map. Sharpening a local map uses this map, sharpening a tower keeps its length and applies sharpening to its levels, arrows and centers, and sharpening an input keeps its given sharp torsion-freeness and induced finite affine cover. Given a monoscheme rule $R$ and fan rule $Q$, a rule-sharpening datum identifies each sharpened resolution of $R$ with the resolution of $Q$ over the canonical sharp base identification. It satisfies naturality equations for the contraction indices and the sharpened comparison maps. This defines data and conditions; it does not assert existence of a rule, a rule-sharpening datum, or a bijection of rules.
